Elder statesman and National Leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, has died at the age of 100. Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, announced his death in a statement personally issued on Tuesday, in Akure, the state capital. Fasoranti, a prominent politician, educationist and pro-democracy activist, was widely respected for his contributions to Nigeria’s political development and his advocacy for Yoruba interests. Here are things to know about the late Afenifere leader. 1. Early Life and Education Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti was born on May 11, 1926, in Akure, Ondo State. He attained the age of 100 in May 2026. He pursued a career in education, studying at the University College, Ibadan, now the University of Ibadan. He also obtained a postgraduate diploma in education from the University of Hull in the United Kingdom and a master’s degree in education administration and school management from Macquarie University in Australia. 2. Career as a Teacher and Educationist Before becoming a prominent figure in Nigerian politics, Fasoranti worked as a teacher and school administrator. His commitment to education remained an important part of his public life. He later established schools, including Omolere Nursery School and Akure High School, contributing to educational development in Ondo State. 3. Political Career and Awoist Ideology Fasoranti was a committed follower of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo and the progressive political tradition associated with him. He was involved in the Action Group during the First Republic and later became associated with the Unity Party of Nigeria during the Second Republic. Between 1979 and 1983, he served as Commissioner for Finance in the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin in the old Ondo State. 4. Leadership of Afenifere Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Following the death of Pa Abraham Adesanya, Fasoranti emerged as the leader of the organisation and became a prominent voice on issues affecting the Yoruba people and Nigeria. His emergence placed him at the centre of the organisation’s efforts to promote Yoruba interests, democratic governance and political restructuring. He led Afenifere through periods of internal disagreements and divisions over leadership and political direction. In 2021, at the age of 95, he appointed Chief Ayo Adebanjo as acting leader and Oba Oladipo Olaitan as deputy leader while retaining his position as substantive National Leader. Despite internal differences within the organisation, Fasoranti remained an influential elder statesman whose views attracted attention from political leaders across the country. Under his leadership, Afenifere continued to advocate restructuring, federalism, good governance and greater equity in the Nigerian federation. 5. During the military dictatorship of the late General Sani Abacha, he remained associated with pro-democracy advocacy and was reported to have survived an assassination attempt linked to the regime. His political activism contributed to his reputation as a defender of democratic principles and constitutional governance. 6. Personal Tragedy Fasoranti suffered a major personal loss in July 2019 when his daughter, Funke Olakunrin, was killed in an attack along the Ondo-Ore Expressway. Olakunrin was killed by gunmen along the Ondo-Ore Expressway, an incident that generated widespread condemnation and renewed national debate about insecurity. The tragedy brought national attention to Fasoranti’s family and prompted expressions of sympathy from political leaders and other Nigerians. Despite the loss, the elder statesman continued to occupy a prominent place in Yoruba political and cultural life. Her death attracted widespread condemnation and renewed national debate about insecurity, particularly attacks on travellers along major highways. Despite the tragedy, Fasoranti remained a respected elder statesman whose views continued to feature in national discussions. Fasoranti married Frances Oladiwura Awosika in 1955. She died in 1991, and he did not remarry. 7. Recognition at 100 Fasoranti marked his 100th birthday on May 11, 2026, drawing tributes from political leaders and prominent Nigerians. President Bola Tinubu described him as an elder statesman, administrator, pro-democracy activist and prominent Afenifere leader, praising his contributions to public service and the country. Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa also celebrated his centenary, describing him as a patriot whose life reflected integrity, courage and commitment to societal development. 8. Advocacy for Restructuring and Good Governance Throughout his public life, Fasoranti consistently advocated restructuring and true federalism, arguing for a political system that would promote fairness, accountability and balanced development. His interventions on national issues reflected his belief in democratic governance, justice and the protection of citizens’ rights. 9. A Legacy of Public Service Fasoranti’s life spanned Nigeria’s colonial period, independence, military rule and the return to democratic government. His contributions as an educationist, politician, pro-democracy activist and Afenifere leader made him an influential figure in Yoruba political history. His death at 100 marks the end of a century-long life associated with public service, political activism and advocacy for good governance. The late Afenifere leader is survived by his children and other family members.
